gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 11 build entry now runs the gpio_wdt, bcm2835_wdt, and dw_wdt starter tests together with the dw_wdt verify and survey gates so the simple-driver watchdog tranche stays reviewable in one place.

A dedicated survey gate now records that the dw_wdt starter, teardown-parity replay, platform-resource preflight, registration-facing handoff, and bounded platform-registration scaffold already exist while keeping the remaining simple-driver roadmap gap explicit instead of letting the current scaffold overclaim parity.

The survey note now anchors the live dw_wdt lane to current `master` `75f8336c4305beed127d7abfae37d3999b7cc57c` so later runs can extend the same Phase 11 slice without rediscovering whether the platform-resource preflight, registration-facing handoff, platform-registration scaffold, and simple-driver roadmap gap already landed.

The bounded starter already derives fixed TOP timeout windows, mirrors reset-mode versus IRQ-mode timeout selection and pretimeout bookkeeping, and now exposes a probe-time summary alongside register-image transitions without claiming platform-backed behavior.

The bounded starter now keeps platform resource preflight reviewable by naming named `tclk` versus shared-clock fallback, optional APB clock presence, optional reset-control and pretimeout-IRQ availability, and the explicit blocked-no-timer-clock posture before any live `devm_*` acquisition lands.

Dedicated Phase 11 tests now keep the bounded platform-resource preflight surface explicit inside the shared DesignWare packet, while the starter-local and verify-backed replays in that same packet carry fixed-top selection, timeout-mode bookkeeping, restart intent, non-stoppable stop semantics, and registration-facing handoff outputs without overstating what this one test file proves by itself.
The slice note now records the exact starter contract so the repo does not blur the current in-memory driver model into clock, reset, IRQ, debugfs, or hardware-backed parity.

The starter now includes a tiny probe-time summary around fixed-versus-custom TOP sourcing, nowayout and restart-priority bookkeeping, stop-on-reboot intent, and already-running watchdog state before any platform-backed behavior lands.

The bounded starter now keeps watchdog info selection, parent linkage, timeout-programming intent, and register-device handoff reviewable after the probe summary without claiming live clock, reset, IRQ, or MMIO work.

The paired registration-scaffold replay now keeps the pre-registration ordering explicit by naming timer-clock path choice, optional APB clock presence, reset-release posture, timeout-programming versus imported-running-state branching, drvdata publication, restart-priority sequencing, stop-on-reboot intent, and bounded register-device request ordering without claiming live platform execution.

The paired verify replay now covers the roadmap teardown and failure-mode parity split by keeping reset-controlled remove, unstoppable hardware running remove, idle remove without a fabricated heartbeat, idle remove with reset-backed quiesce, idle stop outcomes across reset-controlled and non-stoppable hardware, idle IRQ-configured teardown without a fabricated stop path or continued heartbeat, IRQ-mode teardown outcomes, and the bounded platform handoff summary reviewable beside the starter.

The bounded starter now attaches the existing platform-resource preflight, registration-facing handoff, and registration-order proof to a truthful platform-registration scaffold by naming `module_platform_driver` plus the `dw_wdt_drv_probe`, `dw_wdt_drv_remove`, and `dw_wdt_drv_shutdown` anchors without claiming live platform-driver execution, clock ownership, or MMIO behavior.

Live IRQ registration, suspend and resume handling, debugfs support, devicetree TOP acquisition, clock and reset ownership, and hardware-backed MMIO validation stay deferred until the lane chooses one real platform-backed probe or remove execution slice to build on top of the newly-landed scaffold.
